name: Tricuspid Valve Agenesis
aliases: Congenital Absence of the Tricuspid Valve

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Clinical and Echocardiographic Diagnostic Criteria for Tricuspid Valve Agenesis

criteria.description: Complete absence of the tricuspid valve confirmed by echocardiography or cardiac MRI
Hypoplasia or underdevelopment of the right ventricle on imaging studies
Presence of an atrial septal defect or patent foramen ovale allowing right-to-left shunting
Central cyanosis observed clinically in the neonatal period
Characteristic systolic murmur due to abnormal blood flow through the heart

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of absent tricuspid valve plus right ventricular hypoplasia and atrial septal defect confirmed by imaging
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis is primarily based on echocardiographic findings supported by clinical presentation.

pathognomonic.notes: Bluish discoloration of skin and mucous membranes due to hypoxemia
Underdeveloped right ventricle detected on imaging
Confirmed by echocardiography or cardiac MRI
searchTerms: absent valve between right atrium and ventricle

common.notes: Due to abnormal intracardiac blood flow
Rapid breathing secondary to cardiac insufficiency
Enlarged liver due to venous congestion
Reduced ability to perform physical activity

occasional.notes: Swelling of lower extremities due to right heart failure
Irregular heart rhythms detected on ECG
Increased red blood cell mass secondary to hypoxia

rare.notes: Stroke or transient ischemic attacks secondary to paradoxical emboli
Abdominal fluid accumulation from right heart failure
Rare fatal arrhythmias or heart failure

laboratory: Elevated hematocrit and hemoglobin due to secondary polycythemia
imaging: Echocardiography demonstrating absent tricuspid valve and right ventricular hypoplasia
Chest X-ray showing cardiomegaly and pulmonary vascular markings
genetic: No specific gene identified; sporadic congenital defect
other: Electrocardiogram showing right atrial enlargement and arrhythmias

distinguishingFeatures: Presence of a fibrous tricuspid valve remnant rather than complete absence
Similar clinical presentation but distinct echocardiographic findings
Apical displacement of the septal leaflet of the tricuspid valve
Presence of a malformed but present tricuspid valve

redFlags: Severe central cyanosis in the neonatal period
Signs of congestive heart failure in infancy
Sudden onset of arrhythmias or syncope
references: Anderson RH, et al. Paediatric Cardiology. 4th ed. Churchill Livingstone; 2010.
Moller JH, et al. Congenital Heart Disease in Adults. Wiley-Blackwell; 2013.
